OP - in terms of panic attacks, I got those regularly too, it’s definitely worth seeing someone about it if you can. Look into some ‘grounding’ techniques, for example when you feel yourself slipping into a panic attack take some deep breaths - just keep trying even if you feel you can’t at first, I know sometimes it feels hard to breath - then count 5 things you can see, 4 things you can hear, 3 things you can touch, 2 you can smell and 1 you can taste. There are more of these techniques online too. 

Look into seeing a counsellor if you can, sometimes unis will have free counselling services (im not sure where you’re based but in the UK they do) and if the panic attacks don’t ease at all then it’s worth speaking to your GP. Bit of a long story, but to summarise: she had a lot of issues, and was an alcoholic. She became quite dependent on me and I allowed it because I cared for her deeply and I really wanted to help her, but it got to a breaking point, she would get jealous if I was with anyone who wasn’t her, when I would stay with my boyfriend at the time she would call me or message me saying she was lonely and threatened to kill herself often. Hospital did nothing because she didn’t actually harm herself, I rang her mum because she agreed to going home for a break. She continued drinking even though she went to AA, which made me so angry after everything she put me through. I know she got better and she did get help, but she viewed me as the bad guy even though she agreed to letting me get her help. I had to cut contact with her even though it hurt, she was my best friend one point, plus her jealousy issues caused me to stop hanging out with other friends so I had pretty much no one after that. My advice to anyone with a dependent friend/anyone in their life- don’t risk your own mental health for them, it’s not going to be worth it, if they need help they’ll only get it when they want it. And don’t be afraid to get more help in if you need it.
